papers.title_original: Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in individuals previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive, addressing the need for updated vaccines against circulating variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 3 master study was conducted in healthy 18- to 55-year-olds, divided into three cohorts: those previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 (cohorts 1-2) and those who were vaccine-naive (cohort 3).
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed through geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of neutralizing titers and seroresponse percentages, while reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were monitored.
analysis.main_results: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1, GMRs after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses were 2.87 and 2.64, respectively, compared with one BNT162b2 dose. Seroresponse differences were 29.0% and 21.0% for one and two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrated that BNT162b2-BA.1 induced higher neutralizing titers and greater seroresponse rates compared to the original vaccine, indicating its potential to improve immune responses against the Omicron BA.1 variant.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may enhance protection against emerging variants, supporting their use in booster campaigns and informing future vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to individuals aged 18-55 years, and the evidence is based on immunogenicity measures rather than clinical outcomes, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in 18- to 55-year-olds previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive. The phase 3 master study compared the vaccine's performance against the original BNT162b2 vaccine, showing higher neutralizing titers and seroresponse rates in vaccinated individuals. In vaccine-naive participants, the BA.1-adapted vaccine also met superiority and noninferiority criteria. Safety profiles were similar between the vaccines. The results suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may improve immune responses against the Omicron variant, supporting their use in booster campaigns. However, the study's focus on immunogenicity rather than clinical outcomes limits its generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 BA.1 适应的 BNT162b2 疫苗 在之前接种过 BNT162b2 疫苗或未接种过 疫苗 的个体中的免疫原性、耐受性和安全性,解决针对循环变异的更新 疫苗 的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 18 至 55 岁健康人群中进行了一项 3 期主研究,分为三组 队列研究:之前接种过 BNT162b2 疫苗的人 (队列研究 1-2) 和未接种过 疫苗 的人 (队列研究 3)。
elements_zh.methods: 通过中和滴度和血清反应百分比的几何平均比(GMR)评估免疫原性,同时监测反应原性和不良事件频率。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in individuals previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive, addressing the need for updated vaccines against circulating variants.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A phase 3 master study was conducted in healthy 18- to 55-year-olds, divided into three cohorts: those previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 (cohorts 1-2) and those who were vaccine-naive (cohort 3).
analysis_en.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed through geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of neutralizing titers and seroresponse percentages, while reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were monitored.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1, GMRs after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses were 2.87 and 2.64, respectively, compared with one BNT162b2 dose. Seroresponse differences were 29.0% and 21.0% for one and two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrated that BNT162b2-BA.1 induced higher neutralizing titers and greater seroresponse rates compared to the original vaccine, indicating its potential to improve immune responses against the Omicron BA.1 variant.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may enhance protection against emerging variants, supporting their use in booster campaigns and informing future vaccine development strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to individuals aged 18-55 years, and the evidence is based on immunogenicity measures rather than clinical outcomes, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

papers.title_zh: Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Variant-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can induce more robust immune responses against closely matched circulating variants than original vaccines. METHODS: Within a phase 3 master study, monovalent Omicron BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 (BNT162b2-BA.1) was evaluated in healthy BNT162b2-experienced (cohorts 1-2) or COVID-19 vaccine-naive (cohort 3) 18 to 55 year-olds. Primary immunogenicity endpoints in cohort 1 were geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Omicron BA.1 neutralizing titers 1 month after BNT162b2-BA.1 to those after one BNT162b2 dose and differences in percentages of participants with Omicron BA.1 seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2. In cohort 2, primary immunogenicity objectives (participants without evidence of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection) were to demonstrate superiority (GMR two-sided 95% CI lower limit > 1) with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse difference (difference two-sided 95% CI lower limit > - 5%) for BNT162b2-BA.1 versus BNT162b2. In cohort 3, primary immunogenicity objectives were to demonstrate superiority with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse after two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses compared with participants receiving BNT162b2 in an efficacy trial. Reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were determined. RESULTS: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1 (BNT162b2-experienced), GMRs compared with one BNT162b2 dose were 2.87 and 2.64 after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively, and differences in percentages of participants with seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 were 29.0% and 21.0% for one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses. In cohort 2 (BNT162b2-experienced), one BNT162b2-BA.1 dose met prespecified superiority and noninferiority criteria with respect to GMR and difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse, respectively, compared with BNT162b2. In cohort 3 (COVID-19 vaccine-naive), superiority with respect to GMR and noninferiority with respect to difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse of BNT162b2-BA.1 to BNT162b2 were met. BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 safety and tolerability profiles were similar. CONCLUSIONS: Omicron BA.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can broaden immune responses against Omicron BA.1 SARS-CoV-2 variants. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT04955626.

papers.title: Efficacy of a psychotherapeutic group intervention for patients with Post-COVID-19 condition: a randomized controlled trial (PsyLoCo study)
papers.abstract: Persistent physical symptoms such as fatigue following SARS-CoV-2 infection are common and often accompanied by cognitive complaints. Alongside biological mechanisms, psychosocial processes can contribute to symptom persistence. Psychotherapeutic interventions could be beneficial in symptom reduction. However, evidence of group-based psychotherapies tailored to Post-COVID-19 condition (PCS) remains limited. In this randomized waitlist-controlled crossover study in an outpatient psychosomatic setting, adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and persisting functionally impairing symptoms were randomized to immediate group psychotherapeutic treatment (intervention group, IG) or treatment as usual with delayed group treatment (control/waitlist group, CG). The intervention comprised 10 bi-weekly manual-guided group sessions (50 min) covering psychoeducation, somatic symptom processing, emotional regulation, and social reintegration. Primary outcome was somatic symptom burden (SSS-8). Secondary outcomes were depressive symptoms (PHQ-9) and anxiety symptoms (GAD-7). Childhood maltreatment (CTS) was examined as a moderator. Efficacy in the randomized phase was tested using ANCOVA comparing post-treatment outcomes in the IG with post-waiting outcomes in the CG, adjusted for baseline severity. Three-month follow-up assessments were analyzed descriptively and exploratorily. Trial registration: https://osf.io/tdn38/overview on Feb 13, 2024 and German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00040598, registered on 12th June 2026. Retrospectively registered. Forty-eight patients were included (IG n = 21; CG n = 27; mean age 53.3 years; 68.8% females). At baseline, somatic symptom burden was high (SSS-8 M = 15.21; SD = 5.62) with clinically relevant depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 M = 10.94, SD = 4.61) and moderate anxiety (GAD-7 M = 7.22; SD = 4.38). Fatigue-related physical exhaustion and cognitive complaints were the most prominent symptoms. No significant efficacy of the psychotherapeutic group intervention over TAU was observed for SSS-8 (β = − 2.20, SE = 1.25, 95% CI [− 4.77, 0.38], t(27) = − 1.75, p = .091), PHQ-9 (β = − 1.77, SE = 1.51, 95% CI [− 4.87, 1.33], t(26) = − 1.18, p = .251), or GAD-7 (β = − 0.81, SE = 1.47, 95% CI [− 3.84, 2.22], t(26) = − 0.55, p = .588) comparing post-treatment outcomes in the IG with post-waiting outcomes in the CG. Baseline symptom severity robustly predicted post-randomization outcomes during the randomized phase (p < .001). CTS was no moderator for the intervention effect. In this exploratory randomized controlled trial, the intervention did not show significant superiority over the control condition; findings should be interpreted cautiously given limited statistical power. Future psychotherapeutic group interventions for patients with PCS have to consider outcome measures beyond severity of persistent physical symptoms rather than evaluating global symptom scores. Group-based psychotherapeutic approaches might benefit from flexibility in adaptation for individual patients’ needs. Stratification by baseline severity and dominant symptom profiles (e.g., fatigue severity, trauma history) may improve sensitivity to clinically meaningful change. Trial registration: DRKS German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00040598, registered on 12th June 2026. Retrospectively registered.

analysis.summary_en: This randomized controlled trial investigated the efficacy of a psychotherapeutic group intervention for patients with Post-COVID-19 condition (PCS). The study included 48 adults with persisting functionally impairing symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection, randomized to immediate group treatment or delayed treatment. The intervention consisted of 10 bi-weekly sessions covering psychoeducation, somatic symptom processing, emotional regulation, and social reintegration. No significant efficacy was observed for somatic symptom burden, depressive symptoms, or anxiety symptoms compared to treatment as usual. Baseline symptom severity predicted outcomes, but childhood maltreatment did not moderate the intervention effect. The study highlights the need for future interventions to consider broader outcome measures and individualized adaptations.

papers.title_zh: Efficacy of a psychotherapeutic group intervention for patients with Post-COVID-19 condition: a randomized controlled trial (PsyLoCo study)
papers.source_body_en: Persistent physical symptoms such as fatigue following SARS-CoV-2 infection are common and often accompanied by cognitive complaints. Alongside biological mechanisms, psychosocial processes can contribute to symptom persistence. Psychotherapeutic interventions could be beneficial in symptom reduction. However, evidence of group-based psychotherapies tailored to Post-COVID-19 condition (PCS) remains limited. In this randomized waitlist-controlled crossover study in an outpatient psychosomatic setting, adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and persisting functionally impairing symptoms were randomized to immediate group psychotherapeutic treatment (intervention group, IG) or treatment as usual with delayed group treatment (control/waitlist group, CG). The intervention comprised 10 bi-weekly manual-guided group sessions (50 min) covering psychoeducation, somatic symptom processing, emotional regulation, and social reintegration. Primary outcome was somatic symptom burden (SSS-8). Secondary outcomes were depressive symptoms (PHQ-9) and anxiety symptoms (GAD-7). Childhood maltreatment (CTS) was examined as a moderator. Efficacy in the randomized phase was tested using ANCOVA comparing post-treatment outcomes in the IG with post-waiting outcomes in the CG, adjusted for baseline severity. Three-month follow-up assessments were analyzed descriptively and exploratorily. Trial registration: https://osf.io/tdn38/overview on Feb 13, 2024 and German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00040598, registered on 12th June 2026. Retrospectively registered. Forty-eight patients were included (IG n = 21; CG n = 27; mean age 53.3 years; 68.8% females). At baseline, somatic symptom burden was high (SSS-8 M = 15.21; SD = 5.62) with clinically relevant depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 M = 10.94, SD = 4.61) and moderate anxiety (GAD-7 M = 7.22; SD = 4.38). Fatigue-related physical exhaustion and cognitive complaints were the most prominent symptoms. No significant efficacy of the psychotherapeutic group intervention over TAU was observed for SSS-8 (β = − 2.20, SE = 1.25, 95% CI [− 4.77, 0.38], t(27) = − 1.75, p = .091), PHQ-9 (β = − 1.77, SE = 1.51, 95% CI [− 4.87, 1.33], t(26) = − 1.18, p = .251), or GAD-7 (β = − 0.81, SE = 1.47, 95% CI [− 3.84, 2.22], t(26) = − 0.55, p = .588) comparing post-treatment outcomes in the IG with post-waiting outcomes in the CG. Baseline symptom severity robustly predicted post-randomization outcomes during the randomized phase (p < .001). CTS was no moderator for the intervention effect. In this exploratory randomized controlled trial, the intervention did not show significant superiority over the control condition; findings should be interpreted cautiously given limited statistical power. Future psychotherapeutic group interventions for patients with PCS have to consider outcome measures beyond severity of persistent physical symptoms rather than evaluating global symptom scores. Group-based psychotherapeutic approaches might benefit from flexibility in adaptation for individual patients’ needs. Stratification by baseline severity and dominant symptom profiles (e.g., fatigue severity, trauma history) may improve sensitivity to clinically meaningful change. Trial registration: DRKS German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00040598, registered on 12th June 2026. Retrospectively registered.

papers.title: Computational prioritization of RBD-targeting nanobodies across SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages, followed by rational biparatopic design and targeted experimental validation.
papers.abstract: The ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron sublineages harboring extensive RBD mutations, compromises the effectiveness of many existing neutralizing nanobodies. Here, we present an integrated computational-experimental framework to prioritize nanobodies with favorable predicted interaction profiles across mutated RBD backgrounds and to explore their potential for biparatopic engineering. Thirty-two nanobody-RBD complexes from the Protein Data Bank were computationally screened across eight Omicron sublineages (BA.1-XBB.1.5). Selected nanobodies were then further evaluated against the Wuhan reference strain and XBB.1.5-the predominant sublineage at the onset of laboratory testing-using molecular simulations and conventional virus neutralization tests (cVNTs) performed in three biological replicates. These analyses led to the prioritization of MR17 and Sb14. In subsequent cVNT assays, MR17 showed a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than against the Wuhan reference strain, whereas Sb14 showed comparable titers against both targets. A biparatopic Sb14-MR17 construct exhibited a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than either monomeric nanobody. In addition, the interaction profiles of selected candidates with the emerging NB.1.8.1 RBD were evaluated computationally. Collectively, these results highlight multi-sublineage computational triage, together with targeted experimental validation, as a practical strategy for prioritizing nanobody candidates under ongoing SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of SARS-CoV-2 evolution, particularly Omicron sublineages with RBD mutations that reduce nanobody efficacy. Researchers developed a computational-experimental framework to screen nanobodies across eight Omicron sublineages, prioritizing MR17 and Sb14 through molecular simulations and neutralization tests. MR17 showed higher neutralization against XBB.1.5 than the Wuhan strain, while Sb14 had comparable titers. A biparatopic Sb14-MR17 construct outperformed both monomers against XBB.1.5. The study demonstrates computational triage combined with experimental validation as an effective strategy for developing nanobodies against evolving variants, with biparatopic designs offering enhanced neutralization potential.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的正在进行的 进化,特别是含有广泛 RBD 突变 的 Omicron 亚系,损害了许多现有中和纳米体的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们提出了一个集成的计算实验框架,以优先考虑在突变 RBD 背景下具有有利预测相互作用特征的纳米抗体,并探索其双互补位工程的潜力。
elements_zh.methods: 通过计算筛选了蛋白质数据库中的 32 种纳米抗体-RBD 复合物,涵盖 8 个 Omicron 亚系 (BA.1-XBB.1.5)。然后,使用分子模拟和在三个生物重复中进行的常规病毒中和测试(cVNT),针对武汉参考毒株和 XBB.1.5 进一步评估选定的纳米抗体。
elements_zh.main_results: 这些分析确定了 MR17 和 Sb14 的优先顺序。在随后的 cVNT 测定中,MR17 对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度显着高于对武汉参考菌株的中和滴度,而 Sb14 对两个靶标的滴度相当。双互补位 Sb14-MR17 构建体表现出比任一单体纳米抗体显着更高的针对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总的来说,这些结果强调了多亚系计算分类以及有针对性的实验验证,作为在持续的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原漂移下优先考虑纳米抗体候选者的实用策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现证明了双互补位纳米抗体构建体增强对不断发展的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的中和作用的潜力,为开发针对当前和未来 Omicron 亚谱系的更有效疗法提供了一种有前途的方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在体外使用计算预测进行的,并且仅限于特定的纳米抗体候选物和病毒亚谱系,这可能会限制研究结果对所有潜在变异或治疗背景的普遍性。

papers.title: Effects of COVID-19 Control Policies on Malaria Surveillance: A Comparative Analysis of North and South Korea.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Both South and North Korea are identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having the potential to eliminate malaria. However, the increase in malaria cases during the COVID-19 response has prompted an investigation into the reasons behind this unexpected rise. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Epidemiological, entomological, and meteorological data from national and international surveillance systems were analyzed. Using the WHO's analytical framework, which can be effectively applied during the elimination phase, we assessed drivers of malaria resurgence in North and South Korea. RESULTS: In North Korea, border closures caused a severe shortage of rapid diagnostic test kits, reducing malaria testing by over 90% by 2021. Microscopy use increased but remained insufficient, while confirmed cases rose from 1819 in 2020 to 3160 in 2023. In South Korea, public health resources were diverted to COVID-19, weakening malaria control activities. The response time for epidemiological investigations increased from 1.3 days in 2019 to 4.3 days in 2021. Relapse cases, which were zero in 2021, increased to eight in 2023, and confirmed cases rose from 274 in 2021 to 673 in 2023. There were no meaningful changes in the drivers of malaria resurgence, including importation of malaria parasites or human susceptibility. With no notable shifts in vector density, variations in temperature and precipitation did not explain the rise in either country, and there were no reports of emerging resistance to insecticides or antimalarial drugs. CONCLUSION: These COVID-19-related disruptions, including supply chain failures and the diversion of human resources, impaired malaria control in countries on the Korean Peninsula.

analysis.methods: The study used the WHO's analytical framework to assess drivers of malaria resurgence, analyzing data on testing availability, response times, and confirmed cases in both countries.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that disruptions caused by the COVID-19 response, such as supply chain failures and resource diversion, were the main drivers of the observed malaria resurgence, with no meaningful changes in the biological factors like vector density or drug resistance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of maintaining malaria surveillance and control efforts during public health emergencies, as resource diversion and logistical challenges can significantly impact disease management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level data, and the evidence is based on reported changes in testing availability and response times, which may not fully capture the complexity of malaria resurgence. The evidence strength is moderate.

papers.title: JN.1-adapted vaccination is associated with readjustment of ancestral memory B cells toward neutralization within the JN.1 antigenic space
papers.abstract: The antigenic drift of SARS-CoV-2 toward the JN.1 lineage has prompted the development of variant-adapted COVID-19 booster vaccines. However, these boosters are thought to primarily recall pre-existing memory B cells (MBC), raising concerns about their ability to realign the immune response in highly pre-exposed populations. Here we analyze antibody and B cell responses in pre-exposed individuals (n = 42; median 4.5 prior COVID-19 vaccinations; 90% with at least one prior SARS-CoV-2 infection) following vaccination with a JN.1-adapted mRNA vaccine. Vaccination is associated with increased IgG binding and enhanced neutralization of JN.1 and related descendant variants. Longitudinal profiling of antigen-specific MBC shows that Wu01-only and Wu01/JN.1 cross-reactive cells remain dominant, while JN.1-only cells modestly increase by day 21. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of antigen-specific MBC in a representative sub-cohort (n = 7), combined with functional monoclonal antibody analyses, demonstrates that somatic hypermutation (SHM) drives intra-clonotype specialization toward improved JN.1 binding and neutralization. These findings indicate maturation of pre-existing, class-switched MBC rather than substantial de novo recruitment of naïve B cells. In conclusion, JN.1-adapted booster vaccination is associated with refinement of pre-existing MBC repertoires toward the JN.1 antigenic space and with enhanced neutralization of contemporary and antigenically proximate variants.

JN.1-adapted vaccination is associated with readjustment of ancestral memory B cells toward neutralization within the JN.1 antigenic space.
source_records.abstract: The antigenic drift of SARS-CoV-2 toward the JN.1 lineage has prompted the development of variant-adapted COVID-19 booster vaccines. However, these boosters are thought to primarily recall pre-existing memory B cells (MBC), raising concerns about their ability to realign the immune response in highly pre-exposed populations. Here we analyze antibody and B cell responses in pre-exposed individuals (n = 42; median 4.5 prior COVID-19 vaccinations; 90% with at least one prior SARS-CoV-2 infection) following vaccination with a JN.1-adapted mRNA vaccine. Vaccination is associated with increased IgG binding and enhanced neutralization of JN.1 and related descendant variants. Longitudinal profiling of antigen-specific MBC shows that Wu01-only and Wu01/JN.1 cross-reactive cells remain dominant, while JN.1-only cells modestly increase by day 21. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of antigen-specific MBC in a representative sub-cohort (n = 7), combined with functional monoclonal antibody analyses, demonstrates that somatic hypermutation (SHM) drives intra-clonotype specialization toward improved JN.1 binding and neutralization. These findings indicate maturation of pre-existing, class-switched MBC rather than substantial de novo recruitment of naïve B cells. In conclusion, JN.1-adapted booster vaccination is associated with refinement of pre-existing MBC repertoires toward the JN.1 antigenic space and with enhanced neutralization of contemporary and antigenically proximate variants.

papers.title: Military Spouse Perceptions of Healthcare Access in Okinawa During the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Introduction During the COVID-19 pandemic, geographic isolation, host-nation healthcare limitations, and broader geopolitical considerations contributed to limited access to care for dependents of active duty service members in Okinawa. This research explored perceived healthcare access barriers among military spouses in Okinawa, Japan, during the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency and identified potential demographic and structural factors associated with perceived access and wellness outcomes. Materials and methods This study used a cross-sectional online survey from February to May 2023 during the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency. Ethical approval was received from the University of Nebraska Medical Center. The 35-item instrument captured demographics, healthcare utilization, access barriers, and wellness perceptions. Access to emergency, urgent, routine, specialty, and preventive care was assessed against TRICARE standards, with percentages calculated to indicate whether benchmarks were met across demographic groups. Logistic regression evaluated associations between age, sponsor rank, and MTF assignment with access outcomes. Results Emergency care met TRICARE standards for 90% of respondents, but fewer met urgent (19%), routine (17%), specialty (25%), or preventive care (47%) benchmarks. Only 22% of spouses perceived they could access care when needed. Younger spouses (19-30) and those assigned to Kadena's 18th Medical Group reported the lowest access. Nearly half reported worsened mental health, and 40% reported food or medical cutbacks. Enlisted spouses were disproportionately affected. Conclusions Military spouses in Okinawa perceived significant barriers to healthcare access during the COVID-19 pandemic, with military treatment facility (MTF) enrollment, sponsor rank, and age emerging as the most consistent factors associated with disparity. Policy implications include the need to provide military families with adequate and accurate information on MTF access to care wait times and civilian healthcare availability before arrival at a new duty station. These findings highlight the need for further research examining military spouse healthcare access in overseas and remote locations.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: This study examined healthcare access barriers among military spouses in Okinawa, Japan, during the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency, focusing on demographic and structural factors associated with perceived access and wellness outcomes.
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 2023 年 2 月至 5 月进行了一项横断面在线调查,使用包含 35 个项目的工具来捕获人口统计数据、医疗保健利用率、准入障碍和健康认知。根据 TRICARE 标准评估急诊、紧急、常规、专业和预防性护理的获得情况,并使用逻辑回归评估年龄、申办者等级和 MTF 分配与获得结果之间的关联。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 冲绳的军人配偶认为,在 新型冠状病毒感染 大流行期间,获得医疗服务存在重大障碍。90% 的受访者的紧急护理符合 TRICARE 标准,但达到紧急护理 (19%)、常规护理 (17%)、专业护理 (25%) 或预防性护理 (47%) 基准的人数较少。只有 22% 的配偶认为他们可以在需要时获得护理,其中年轻配偶(19-30 岁)和分配到嘉手纳第 18 医疗小组的配偶报告获得护理的机会最低。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究强调了医疗保健获取方面的差异,但没有解决潜在的争议或超出已确定障碍的具体证据差距。需要进一步研究来检查海外和偏远地区的军人配偶医疗保健获取情况。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 政策影响包括需要向军人家属提供充分和准确的信息,说明 MTF 在到达新工作地点之前获得护理的等待时间和平民医疗保健的可用性。

Ethical approval was received from the University of Nebraska Medical Center. The 35-item instrument captured demographics, healthcare utilization, access barriers, and wellness perceptions. Access to emergency, urgent, routine, specialty, and preventive care was assessed against TRICARE standards, with percentages calculated to indicate whether benchmarks were met across demographic groups. Logistic regression evaluated associations between age, sponsor rank, and MTF assignment with access outcomes. Results Emergency care met TRICARE standards for 90% of respondents, but fewer met urgent (19%), routine (17%), specialty (25%), or preventive care (47%) benchmarks. Only 22% of spouses perceived they could access care when needed. Younger spouses (19-30) and those assigned to Kadena's 18th Medical Group reported the lowest access. Nearly half reported worsened mental health, and 40% reported food or medical cutbacks. Enlisted spouses were disproportionately affected. Conclusions Military spouses in Okinawa perceived significant barriers to healthcare access during the COVID-19 pandemic, with military treatment facility (MTF) enrollment, sponsor rank, and age emerging as the most consistent factors associated with disparity. Policy implications include the need to provide military families with adequate and accurate information on MTF access to care wait times and civilian healthcare availability before arrival at a new duty station. These findings highlight the need for further research examining military spouse healthcare access in overseas and remote locations.

papers.title: Adiponectin Signaling as an Immunometabolic Regulator in COVID-19: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adiponectin is a pleiotropic adipocytokine with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and insulin-sensitizing functions. Its regulatory role in glucose and lipid metabolism, endothelial homeostasis, and immune responses positions it as a key determinant of immunometabolic resilience. Dysregulated adiponectin signaling has been increasingly implicated in adverse COVID-19 outcomes, particularly among individuals with metabolic comorbidities. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize mechanistic, preclinical, and translational evidence on adiponectin signaling in COVID-19 and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic and lifestyle-modulated target. METHODS: A critical review of published literature on adiponectin biology, AdipoR1/R2 receptor signaling, AMPK and PPAR-α pathways, cytokine regulation, oxidative stress, and infection-induced metabolic reprogramming was conducted. RESULTS: COVID-19 is consistently associated with reduced circulating adiponectin, with the greatest declines observed in obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. Mechanistic and animal studies show that adiponectin activation attenuates hyperinflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and multi-organ injury. These effects are mediated through AMPK activation, PPAR-α modulation, NF-κB suppression, and restoration of metabolic-immune balance. CONCLUSIONS: Adiponectin signaling represents a promising therapeutic target for mitigating COVID-19 severity, especially in metabolically vulnerable populations. Pharmacological agonists and lifestyle interventions that enhance adiponectin pathways warrant further translational investigation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and its associated disease, COVID-19, with an emphasis on understanding adiponectin signaling as an immunometabolic regulator. The central question is to synthesize mechanistic, preclinical, and translational evidence on adiponectin signaling in SARS-CoV-2 infection and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic and lifestyle-modulated target.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a critical analysis of published literature on adiponectin biology, AdipoR1/R2 receptor signaling, AMPK and PPAR-α pathways, cytokine regulation, oxidative stress, and infection-induced metabolic reprogramming. The evidence was sourced from studies on SARS-CoV-2 and related entities, with a focus on mechanistic and animal studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that SARS-CoV-2 infection is consistently associated with reduced circulating adiponectin, particularly in individuals with metabolic comorbidities. Mechanistic and animal studies demonstrate that adiponectin activation can attenuate hyperinflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and multi-organ injury through AMPK activation, PPAR-α modulation, NF-κB suppression, and restoration of metabolic-immune balance. Adiponectin signaling is identified as a promising therapeutic target for mitigating the severity of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that while adiponectin signaling is implicated in adverse outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection, the exact mechanisms and pathways involved remain under investigation. There is a need for more detailed studies on the role of adiponectin in different SARS-CoV-2 variants and in diverse populations to fully understand its therapeutic potential.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that pharmacological agonists and lifestyle interventions that enhance adiponectin pathways should be further explored for their potential in mitigating the severity of SARS-CoV-2 infection. This includes targeted research on metabolic comorbidities and the development of therapies that modulate adiponectin signaling.

The review concludes that adiponectin signaling represents a promising therapeutic target for mitigating the severity of SARS-CoV-2 infection, especially in metabolically vulnerable populations. It emphasizes the need for further research on pharmacological agonists and lifestyle interventions that enhance adiponectin pathways to improve treatment strategies for COVID-19.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对已发表的有关脂联素生物学、AdipoR1/R2 受体信号传导、AMPK 和 PPAR-α 通路、细胞因子调节、氧化应激和感染诱导的代谢重编程的文献进行了批判性分析。证据来源于对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 和相关实体的研究,重点是机制和动物研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染始终与循环脂联素减少相关,特别是在患有代谢合并症的个体中。机制和动物研究表明,脂联素激活可以通过 AMPK 激活、PPAR-α 调节、NF-κB 抑制和恢复代谢免疫平衡来减轻过度炎症、氧化应激、内皮功能障碍和多器官损伤。脂联素信号传导被认为是减轻 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染严重程度的有希望的治疗靶点。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,虽然脂联素信号传导与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的不良后果有关,但所涉及的确切机制和途径仍在研究中。需要对脂联素在不同 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体和不同人群中的作用进行更详细的研究,以充分了解其治疗潜力。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,应进一步探索增强脂联素通路的药理学激动剂和生活方式干预措施在减轻 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染严重程度方面的潜力。这包括对代谢合并症的有针对性的研究以及调节脂联素信号传导的疗法的开发。

papers.title: COVID-19 servicescape and its consequences in the COVID-19 pandemic era
papers.abstract: This study examines the COVID-19 servicescape of cafés and investigates how it affects enjoyment and COVID-19 anxiety, which in turn influence revisit intention. The proposed model is based on the two-factor theory and the cognition-affect-behavior model. Data were collected from online survey panel members and analyzed with SmartPLS 4.0.8. The findings show that, within the physical dimension, atmospherics, menu, and self-service technology positively influence enjoyment. Within the social dimension, uncrowdedness negatively affects enjoyment, whereas sanitary safety and employee service influence enjoyment and revisit intentions only indirectly through COVID-19 anxiety. Complementing these findings, Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) identifies sanitary safety as a necessary condition for revisit intentions despite its nonsignificant direct effect. The study offers both theoretical and practical implications for servicescape management in the pandemic era.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the impact of the COVID-19 servicescape on customer enjoyment and anxiety in cafés, and how these factors influence revisit intention. The study uses SmartPLS 4.0.8 for data analysis, which was collected from an online survey panel. Key findings indicate that physical factors such as atmospherics, menu, and self-service technology positively affect enjoyment, while social factors like uncrowdedness have a negative impact. Sanitary safety, though not directly significant, is identified as a necessary condition for revisit intentions through Necessary Condition Analysis. The research highlights the importance of managing the servicescape during the pandemic to enhance customer experience and encourage repeat visits. The study provides both theoretical and practical insights for servicescape management in the context of the ongoing pandemic.

papers.title: Detecting and supporting COVID-19 outbreak response in a small-scale nursing home through passive wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive wastewater sampling has emerged as a cost-effective approach for pathogen monitoring, but its application in very small populations has not been well studied. This study reports the use of tampons as passive samplers in a small-scale nursing home of 24 residents to detect respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Weekly wastewater surveillance by reverse transcription digital PCR (RT-dPCR) for a 1-year period resulted in a cluster of consecutive SARS-CoV-2 detections over 4 weeks. When wastewater SARS-CoV-2 concentrations reached higher levels in the third and fourth weeks, whole-genome sequencing achieved >98% genome coverage, identifying lineage LB.1.5, while lower-concentration samples produced only partial genomes. Clinical testing was initiated in the fourth week when clinical symptoms also emerged, and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 15 of 24 residents and staff. Sequencing of the clinical samples confirmed LB.1.5 in 11 cases, corroborating the wastewater findings. Influenza A subtypes H3N2 and H1N1 were additionally detected in wastewater by targeted enrichment sequencing, and RSV was detected once by RT-dPCR, neither of which was associated with confirmed clinical cases. These results demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can precede clinical symptoms for early detection, and passive sampling using tampons is a practical and sensitive strategy for outbreak surveillance in small-scale facilities. The study also highlights the need for clear response protocols that include rapid clinical testing and cohorting measures when wastewater viral concentrations exceed defined thresholds. IMPORTANCE Nursing homes are among the highest-risk settings for infectious disease outbreaks, yet early detection remains challenging due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections and limited resources for routine clinical surveillance. This study demonstrates that inexpensive tampon-based passive wastewater samplers can detect SARS-CoV-2 up to 3 weeks before clinical symptoms emerge in a nursing home with only 24 residents, which is the smallest population in which this method has been validated. Wastewater-derived genomes matched clinical sequencing quality, enabling identification of a novel SARS-CoV-2 lineage new to Hawai'i. These findings support passive wastewater surveillance as a practical early warning tool for small congregate care facilities, provided that clear institutional response protocols are in place.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study reports the use of tampons as passive samplers in a small-scale nursing home of 24 residents to detect respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.methods: Weekly wastewater surveillance by reverse transcription digital PCR (RT-dPCR) for a 1-year period resulted in a cluster of consecutive SARS-CoV-2 detections over 4 weeks. When wastewater SARS-CoV-2 concentrations reached higher levels in the third and fourth weeks, whole-genome sequencing achieved >98% genome coverage, identifying lineage LB.1.5, while lower-concentration samples produced only partial genomes.
analysis.main_results: Clinical testing was initiated in the fourth week when clinical symptoms also emerged, and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 15 of 24 residents and staff. Sequencing of the clinical samples confirmed LB.1.5 in 11 cases, corroborating the wastewater findings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can precede clinical symptoms for early detection, and passive sampling using tampons is a practical and sensitive strategy for outbreak surveillance in small-scale facilities. The study also highlights the need for clear response protocols that include rapid clinical testing and cohorting measures when wastewater viral concentrations exceed defined thresholds.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support passive wastewater surveillance as a practical early warning tool for small congregate care facilities, provided that clear institutional response protocols are in place. This study demonstrates that inexpensive tampon-based passive wastewater samplers can detect SARS-CoV-2 up to 3 weeks before clinical symptoms emerge in a nursing home with only 24 residents, which is the smallest population in which this method has been validated.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment. However, the study demonstrates that wastewater-derived genomes matched clinical sequencing quality, enabling identification of a novel SARS-CoV-2 lineage new to Hawai'i.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated passive wastewater surveillance using tampon samplers in a small nursing home with 24 residents to detect SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses. Weekly RT-dPCR testing identified a 4-week cluster of SARS-CoV-2 detections, with whole-genome sequencing revealing lineage LB.1.5 in higher-concentration samples. Clinical testing confirmed infection in 15 residents/staff, with sequencing matching wastewater findings. Wastewater detection preceded symptoms by up to 3 weeks, demonstrating early detection capability. Influenza A and RSV were also detected but not clinically confirmed. The study validates tampon-based wastewater surveillance as a sensitive, cost-effective early warning tool for small facilities, emphasizing the need for clear response protocols when viral thresholds are exceeded.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 被动废水采样已成为病原体监测的一种经济有效的方法,但在极小规模人群中的应用尚未得到充分研究。养老院是传染病暴发风险最高的场所之一,但由于无症状感染率高和常规临床监测资源有限,早期检测仍然具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究报告了在拥有 24 名居民的小型疗养院中使用卫生棉条作为被动采样器来检测呼吸道病毒,包括 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、甲型流感、乙型流感和呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果表明,废水 暴发 可以先于临床症状进行早期检测,并且使用卫生棉条进行被动采样是小型设施中 暴发 暴发 暴发 的实用且敏感的策略。该研究还强调需要制定明确的应对方案,包括当废水病毒浓度超过规定阈值时进行快速临床测试和分组措施。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持被动废水 监测 作为小型聚集护理设施的实用早期预警工具,前提是制定明确的机构应对方案。这项研究表明,廉价的基于卫生棉条的被动废水采样器可以在只有 24 名居民的疗养院出现临床症状之前长达 3 周检测到 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,这是该方法已得到验证的最小人群。

papers.title_zh: Detecting and supporting COVID-19 outbreak response in a small-scale nursing home through passive wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Passive wastewater sampling has emerged as a cost-effective approach for pathogen monitoring, but its application in very small populations has not been well studied. This study reports the use of tampons as passive samplers in a small-scale nursing home of 24 residents to detect respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Weekly wastewater surveillance by reverse transcription digital PCR (RT-dPCR) for a 1-year period resulted in a cluster of consecutive SARS-CoV-2 detections over 4 weeks. When wastewater SARS-CoV-2 concentrations reached higher levels in the third and fourth weeks, whole-genome sequencing achieved >98% genome coverage, identifying lineage LB.1.5, while lower-concentration samples produced only partial genomes. Clinical testing was initiated in the fourth week when clinical symptoms also emerged, and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 15 of 24 residents and staff. Sequencing of the clinical samples confirmed LB.1.5 in 11 cases, corroborating the wastewater findings. Influenza A subtypes H3N2 and H1N1 were additionally detected in wastewater by targeted enrichment sequencing, and RSV was detected once by RT-dPCR, neither of which was associated with confirmed clinical cases. These results demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can precede clinical symptoms for early detection, and passive sampling using tampons is a practical and sensitive strategy for outbreak surveillance in small-scale facilities. The study also highlights the need for clear response protocols that include rapid clinical testing and cohorting measures when wastewater viral concentrations exceed defined thresholds. IMPORTANCE Nursing homes are among the highest-risk settings for infectious disease outbreaks, yet early detection remains challenging due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections and limited resources for routine clinical surveillance. This study demonstrates that inexpensive tampon-based passive wastewater samplers can detect SARS-CoV-2 up to 3 weeks before clinical symptoms emerge in a nursing home with only 24 residents, which is the smallest population in which this method has been validated. Wastewater-derived genomes matched clinical sequencing quality, enabling identification of a novel SARS-CoV-2 lineage new to Hawai'i. These findings support passive wastewater surveillance as a practical early warning tool for small congregate care facilities, provided that clear institutional response protocols are in place.

papers.title: A Novel Older-Adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index to Measure the Transition from Pandemic Mortality to Endemic Resilience in Spain
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic produced a severe and heterogeneous burden across age groups, territories and epidemic phases in Spain. Older adults experienced disproportionately high rates of hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission and death, particularly during the early pandemic waves when vaccination was unavailable. However, the relationship between surveillance-confirmed cases and severe outcomes changed substantially over time, a phenomenon termed epidemiological decoupling. This study developed and applied a novel Older-adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index (O-CSDI) to weekly COVID-19 surveillance data from the 17 Spanish autonomous communities and the two autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla. The integrated dataset covered January 2020 to July 2023 and comprised 3496 autonomous community–week observations and 143 variables obtained from four open-access surveillance sources: ISCIII-RENAVE, Datadista/Ministerio de Sanidad, Our World in Data and the MoMo excess mortality system. However, the primary incidence- and ratio-based O-CSDI analyses were restricted to March 2020–March 2022 because open-access individual event counts were no longer structurally comparable after the transition to reduced surveillance. Data from later periods were retained only for contextual vaccination and MoMo mortality indicators. The O-CSDI quantifies the degree to which reported COVID-19 incidence became disconnected from hospitalization, ICU admission and mortality in adults aged 60–69, 70–79 and ≥80 years. The primary version of the index was based on the death-to-case ratio, while complementary versions examined hospitalization-to-case, ICU-to-hospitalization and death-to-hospitalization transitions. Results showed progressive but heterogeneous decoupling across phases, territorial units and age strata, with the strongest decoupling observed during the Omicron BA.1/BA.2 period and the highest residual mortality burden in adults aged ≥80 years. All results were interpreted as ecological, descriptive indicators rather than individual-level risks or causal estimates. These findings provide a reproducible epidemiological tool for retrospective pandemic evaluation and preparedness in ageing populations.

source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic produced a severe and heterogeneous burden across age groups, territories and epidemic phases in Spain. Older adults experienced disproportionately high rates of hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission and death, particularly during the early pandemic waves when vaccination was unavailable. However, the relationship between surveillance-confirmed cases and severe outcomes changed substantially over time, a phenomenon termed epidemiological decoupling. This study developed and applied a novel Older-adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index (O-CSDI) to weekly COVID-19 surveillance data from the 17 Spanish autonomous communities and the two autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla. The integrated dataset covered January 2020 to July 2023 and comprised 3496 autonomous community–week observations and 143 variables obtained from four open-access surveillance sources: ISCIII-RENAVE, Datadista/Ministerio de Sanidad, Our World in Data and the MoMo excess mortality system. However, the primary incidence- and ratio-based O-CSDI analyses were restricted to March 2020–March 2022 because open-access individual event counts were no longer structurally comparable after the transition to reduced surveillance. Data from later periods were retained only for contextual vaccination and MoMo mortality indicators. The O-CSDI quantifies the degree to which reported COVID-19 incidence became disconnected from hospitalization, ICU admission and mortality in adults aged 60–69, 70–79 and ≥80 years. All results were interpreted as ecological, descriptive indicators rather than individual-level risks or causal estimates. papers.title: Tunneling nanotube-mediated intercellular spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants in epithelial cells reveals a host-targeted antiviral vulnerability.
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 exploits tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) as actin-based conduits for intercellular transmission in epithelial cells. TNT formation was markedly enhanced in the Delta variant compared with the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron strains, consistent with their relative transmissibility. The Delta variant also promoted extensive filopodia and branched TNT networks, facilitating efficient cell-to-cell dissemination. Confocal and ultrastructural analyses revealed active transfer of mitochondria and lysosomes through these nanotubes, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 co-opts host organelle trafficking to support replication and persistence. Pharmacological inhibition of Cdc42-dependent actin remodeling or CaMKII signaling disrupted TNT formation. Collectively, these findings identify TNTs as a crucial pathway for variant-dependent SARS-CoV-2 dissemination in epithelial cells and reveal host cytoskeletal dynamics as a tractable antiviral target for limiting viral spread.

papers.title: Has COVID-19 Exacerbated Ethnic-Related Inequalities in Cancer Care in the UK? Findings from a Narrative Review with a Systematic Search.
papers.abstract: Ethnic inequalities in cancer care have long been a concern in the UK, with minoritised populations facing inequalities in access, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these inequities, worsening barriers to care. This narrative literature review, which incorporates a systematic search, examines the impact of the pandemic on ethnic inequalities in cancer care in the UK. Findings indicate that due to the pandemic, ethnic minority patients experienced lower screening uptake, greater delays in diagnosis, and reduced access to timely treatment. GP referral thresholds were higher for ethnic minority groups, leading to later-stage diagnoses, while emergency presentations and treatment delays were more frequent. Systemic healthcare pressures and communication gaps further contributed to inequalities. Addressing these inequities requires urgent policy interventions, including improved access to screening, equitable referral processes, and culturally sensitive care pathways. Further research is needed to assess post-treatment outcomes and evaluate targeted interventions. As the NHS recovers from the COVID-19 pandemic's disruptions, ensuring equitable access to high-quality cancer care for all ethnic groups must remain a priority.

papers.title: A systematic meta-analytic comparative evaluation of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from test-negative design studies in the Northern Hemisphere pre/post COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.abstract: Background Influenza circulation was substantially reduced during the COVID-19 pandemic. The consequent reduction in population immunity may have resulted in increased influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) after the pandemic via reduced immunity in unvaccinated individuals compared to the pre-pandemic period. Methods We systematically reviewed published peer-reviewed test-negative design (TND) studies of seasonal influenza VE against medically-attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza in the Northern Hemisphere. We compared pooled VE estimates before (2010/11-2019/20) and after (2022/23-2024/25) the COVID-19 pandemic (defined as 2020/21-2021/22). Pooled VE against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), influenza B, and B/Victoria was calculated for three age groups (6 months-17 years, 18-64 years, ≥65 years) using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I 2 statistic, and differences between pooled VE estimates pre- and post-pandemic periods were tested with the χ 2 statistic. Results Eighty-five publications were included. Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) was significantly higher than pre-pandemic VE in 6-month-17-year-olds (53% [42-64%] vs 37% [30-45%]) and 18-64-year-olds (35% [25-45%] vs 21% [13-29%]). Similarly, VE against influenza B was higher post-pandemic in both age groups (85% [78-93%] vs 52% [45-60%] and 73% [59-87%] vs 49% [41-57%], respectively). Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds (37% [27-46%] vs 55% [47-62%]). No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and data for B/Victoria were limited. Conclusions The evidence suggests slightly higher VE against seasonal influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic although there may be factors other than population immunity that may explain our observations.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review evaluates seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in the Northern Hemisphere before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on test-negative design (TND) studies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic meta-analysis of 85 published TND studies comparing pooled VE estimates pre-pandemic (2010/11-2019/20) and post-pandemic (2022/23-2024/25), using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis and heterogeneity quantification (I2 statistic).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) and influenza B was significantly higher in younger age groups (6 months-17 years and 18-64 years), while VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower in 18-64-year-olds; no significant differences were observed in ≥65-year-olds.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Factors other than population immunity may explain observed VE changes; data for B/Victoria were limited, and mechanisms for differential VE by strain and age remain unresolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the impact of reduced population immunity on influenza VE and to investigate strain-specific and age-specific VE dynamics post-pandemic.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic meta-analysis evaluated seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in the Northern Hemisphere before and after the COVID-19 pandemic using test-negative design studies. Eighty-five publications were included, with pooled VE estimates compared across pre-pandemic (2010/11-2019/20) and post-pandemic (2022/23-2024/25) periods. Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) and influenza B was significantly higher in younger age groups, while VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower in 18-64-year-olds. No significant differences were observed in older adults (≥65 years). The authors suggest that reduced population immunity during the pandemic may have contributed to these changes, though other factors may also play a role. Limited data for B/Victoria and unresolved mechanisms for differential VE highlight areas needing further investigation.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review evaluates seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in the Northern Hemisphere before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on test-negative design (TND) studies.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic meta-analysis of 85 published TND studies comparing pooled VE estimates pre-pandemic (2010/11-2019/20) and post-pandemic (2022/23-2024/25), using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis and heterogeneity quantification (I2 statistic).
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) and influenza B was significantly higher in younger age groups (6 months-17 years and 18-64 years), while VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower in 18-64-year-olds; no significant differences were observed in ≥65-year-olds.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Factors other than population immunity may explain observed VE changes; data for B/Victoria were limited, and mechanisms for differential VE by strain and age remain unresolved.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the impact of reduced population immunity on influenza VE and to investigate strain-specific and age-specific VE dynamics post-pandemic.

papers.title_zh: A systematic meta-analytic comparative evaluation of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from test-negative design studies in the Northern Hemisphere pre/post COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.source_body_en: Background Influenza circulation was substantially reduced during the COVID-19 pandemic. The consequent reduction in population immunity may have resulted in increased influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) after the pandemic via reduced immunity in unvaccinated individuals compared to the pre-pandemic period. Methods We systematically reviewed published peer-reviewed test-negative design (TND) studies of seasonal influenza VE against medically-attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza in the Northern Hemisphere. We compared pooled VE estimates before (2010/11-2019/20) and after (2022/23-2024/25) the COVID-19 pandemic (defined as 2020/21-2021/22). Pooled VE against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), influenza B, and B/Victoria was calculated for three age groups (6 months-17 years, 18-64 years, ≥65 years) using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I 2 statistic, and differences between pooled VE estimates pre- and post-pandemic periods were tested with the χ 2 statistic. Results Eighty-five publications were included. Post-pandemic VE against A(H3N2) was significantly higher than pre-pandemic VE in 6-month-17-year-olds (53% [42-64%] vs 37% [30-45%]) and 18-64-year-olds (35% [25-45%] vs 21% [13-29%]). Similarly, VE against influenza B was higher post-pandemic in both age groups (85% [78-93%] vs 52% [45-60%] and 73% [59-87%] vs 49% [41-57%], respectively). Conversely, VE against A(H1N1)pdm09 was lower post-pandemic in 18-64-year-olds (37% [27-46%] vs 55% [47-62%]). No significant differences were observed for ≥65-year-olds, and data for B/Victoria were limited. Conclusions The evidence suggests slightly higher VE against seasonal influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic although there may be factors other than population immunity that may explain our observations.

papers.title: SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae co‐infection during the early COVID‐19 pandemic: diagnostic bias leading to delayed recognition
papers.abstract: Co‐infections during the early COVID‐19 pandemic were frequently under‐recognized due to diagnostic bias, limited availability of pathogen‐specific testing, and the overwhelming clinical focus on SARS‐CoV‐2. We report a case of co‐infection with SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae in a previously healthy 35‐year‐old man who presented with febrile respiratory illness in April 2020. Chest computed tomography demonstrated multiple small ground‐glass opacities, and serology showed a M. pneumoniae PA titer of 1:640, leading clinicians to initially diagnose M. pneumoniae pneumonia. However, when the SARS‐CoV‐2 PCR result was subsequently recognized on day 6 of illness, diagnostic anchoring toward COVID‐19 occurred, and M. pneumoniae was downgraded to a secondary consideration despite supportive radiological and serological evidence. This sequence contributed to premature closure and base‐rate neglect, with co‐infection formally acknowledged only after both results became available. The patient improved with supportive care and appropriate antimicrobial therapy. This case illustrates how cognitive biases and pandemic‐related diagnostic constraints contributed to delayed recognition of co‐infections during the early pandemic. In contrast, current Omicron‐lineage variants exhibit attenuated severity and low ascertainment, making co‐infections in hospitalized patients potentially more clinically significant yet easily overlooked. Awareness of diagnostic pitfalls remains essential for accurate evaluation of respiratory infections in the contemporary era.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports a case of co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae in a previously healthy 35-year-old man during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. The case highlights how diagnostic bias and the overwhelming focus on SARS-CoV-2 led to the initial misdiagnosis of M. pneumoniae pneumonia, with the co-infection only being recognized after both test results were available. The study emphasizes the importance of being aware of diagnostic pitfalls in the context of respiratory infections, particularly during a pandemic. The findings suggest that co-infections may be more clinically significant in the context of Omicron variants, which have lower severity and ascertainment rates, yet remain easily overlooked. The evidence is based on a single case report, which provides a clear example of diagnostic bias but may not be generalizable to broader populations. The study's limitations include its reliance on a single case and the potential for cognitive biases to affect clinical interpretation. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are based on observational data rather than controlled experiments.

papers.title: Sustained Utilization of Video-Based Outpatient Psychiatry Visits Following the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency at an Academic Health Center.
papers.abstract: Background Telepsychiatry expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic to support continuity of psychiatric care, although its long-term durability following the expiration of pandemic-era policies remains uncertain. This study evaluated long-term utilization of telepsychiatry and patient and clinician acceptability within outpatient practice. Methods A repeated cross-sectional electronic health record analysis of outpatient psychiatric visits from 2020 to 2025 compared in-person and virtual visit completion and no-show rates across five annual intervals. Telepsychiatry acceptability was evaluated through a patient survey administered in 2021-2022 ( n = 655) and clinician surveys conducted in 2020 ( n = 50) and 2025 ( n = 38). Results Among 219,007 visits, 44% were in-person and 56% were virtual. The overall no-show rate was 10.46%, with no significant difference between visit types ( p = 0.178). Two intervals demonstrated significant differences: 2021-2022 (virtual = 9.6%, in-person = 11.0%, p p p = 0.037). Most patients agreed that their telepsychiatry visit was as good as in-person (92.4%) and more convenient (97.1%). Provider belief that virtual visits were as effective as in-person decreased from 92.0% in 2020 to 74.3% in 2025 ( p = 0.026). Conclusions Telepsychiatry utilization remains a substantial component of outpatient care. Comparable no-show rates and high patient satisfaction support telepsychiatry as a viable and acceptable modality, although provider enthusiasm appears to have moderated over time.

papers.title: Living with Long Covid: A Qualitative Analysis of Experiences, Coping Strategies and Care across the Illness Journey in Switzerland
papers.abstract: Background Long Covid affects millions worldwide and disrupts the personal, professional, and social lives of those affected. Yet, insights on the day-to-day experience of living with Long Covid, how people adapt to the condition, and how they experience care remain limited. Methods Between November 2024 and February 2025, we recruited people living with Long Covid through Long Covid related studies and patient networks. Data were collected through a one-time semi-structured survey, completed using a speech-to-text feature with automatic transcription, and addressing 1) key events and experiences, 2) coping and support strategies, and 3) advice to others affected. We applied an inductive thematic analysis to develop a framework of key themes. Results We included 137 participants (median age 48 years, 73.7% women, median three years since SARS-CoV-2 infection). Analysis yielded 13 sub-themes within four key themes: medical issues; social, occupational and health care impact; barriers to recovery; and resources and strategies. Participants described a broad range of symptoms, most notably fatigue, cognitive difficulties, post-exertional crashes and psychological symptoms including depression and, in some cases, suicidal thoughts. These symptoms profoundly disrupted their social, working and family lives. In severe cases, independent living became impossible, with social isolation, severely reduced activity, and financial difficulties. Many described a long diagnostic journey in which symptoms were frequently dismissed as psychological and early advice to stay active that worsened their condition. The health care and social security systems were seen as ill-equipped to support people affected by Long Covid. With no effective causal therapies, treatment focused on symptom relief and participants tried many complementary and alternative treatments. Pacing was the only strategy widely used and perceived as effective in preventing crashes, alongside lifestyle adjustment, peer support, and maintaining hope. Conclusion These narrative accounts reveal the multidimensional burden of Long Covid, one that is exacerbated by how affected people are treated within the health and social systems. These findings underscore the need for empathic, knowledgeable care, validation of people’s experiences, and policy frameworks equipped to recognize and support people with Long Covid. Patient or Public Contribution This study is about the lived experiences of people affected by Long Covid. During the conceptualization phase, we consulted three people with lived experience of Long Covid to discuss the relevance of the research questions and study design. All participants received a newsletter with a plain language summary of interim findings. Following completion of this analysis, we conducted a focus group discussion with eight participants to validate our findings, identify gaps, and ensure that the findings accurately reflected their experiences. Feedback from this process informed the final manuscript.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the experiences, coping strategies, and care of people living with Long Covid across the illness journey in Switzerland. The central question focuses on understanding the multidimensional impact of Long Covid on affected individuals' lives and their interactions with healthcare and social systems.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A qualitative study conducted between November 2024 and February 2025, involving 137 participants (median age 48 years, 73.7% women) recruited through Long Covid studies and patient networks. Data were collected via a one-time semi-structured survey using speech-to-text transcription, addressing key events, coping strategies, and advice to others. Inductive thematic analysis was applied to develop a framework of key themes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identified 13 sub-themes within four key themes: medical issues, social/occupational/healthcare impact, barriers to recovery, and resources/strategies. Participants reported profound disruptions to social, working, and family lives due to symptoms like fatigue, cognitive difficulties, and psychological issues. The healthcare and social security systems were perceived as ill-equipped to support Long Covid patients, and diagnostic journeys often involved dismissal of symptoms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights controversies in early advice to stay active, which worsened participants' conditions, and the lack of effective causal therapies. Evidence gaps include limited understanding of how healthcare systems can better support Long Covid patients and the need for more research on effective treatments and interventions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Findings emphasize the need for empathic, knowledgeable care that validates patients' experiences and policy frameworks to recognize and support Long Covid. Pacing was identified as the most effective strategy for preventing crashes, alongside lifestyle adjustments, peer support, and maintaining hope. The study calls for improved healthcare and social security systems to address the multidimensional burden of Long Covid.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores the lived experiences of 137 people with Long Covid in Switzerland, revealing profound impacts on their social, professional, and personal lives. Participants reported diverse symptoms, including fatigue, cognitive difficulties, and psychological distress, often leading to diagnostic delays and dismissed experiences. The healthcare and social systems were perceived as inadequate, with no effective causal therapies available. Pacing emerged as the most effective coping strategy, alongside lifestyle adjustments and peer support. The study underscores the need for empathetic care, validated experiences, and policy frameworks to address the multidimensional burden of Long Covid, highlighting gaps in current healthcare support and treatment options.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review examines the experiences, coping strategies, and care of people living with Long Covid across the illness journey in Switzerland. The central question focuses on understanding the multidimensional impact of Long Covid on affected individuals' lives and their interactions with healthcare and social systems.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A qualitative study conducted between November 2024 and February 2025, involving 137 participants (median age 48 years, 73.7% women) recruited through Long Covid studies and patient networks. Data were collected via a one-time semi-structured survey using speech-to-text transcription, addressing key events, coping strategies, and advice to others. Inductive thematic analysis was applied to develop a framework of key themes.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identified 13 sub-themes within four key themes: medical issues, social/occupational/healthcare impact, barriers to recovery, and resources/strategies. analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights controversies in early advice to stay active, which worsened participants' conditions, and the lack of effective causal therapies. papers.title_zh: 与 长新冠 一起生活:瑞士疾病历程中的经历、应对策略和护理的定性分析
papers.source_body_en: Background Long Covid affects millions worldwide and disrupts the personal, professional, and social lives of those affected. Yet, insights on the day-to-day experience of living with Long Covid, how people adapt to the condition, and how they experience care remain limited. Methods Between November 2024 and February 2025, we recruited people living with Long Covid through Long Covid related studies and patient networks. Data were collected through a one-time semi-structured survey, completed using a speech-to-text feature with automatic transcription, and addressing 1) key events and experiences, 2) coping and support strategies, and 3) advice to others affected. We applied an inductive thematic analysis to develop a framework of key themes. Results We included 137 participants (median age 48 years, 73.7% women, median three years since SARS-CoV-2 infection). Analysis yielded 13 sub-themes within four key themes: medical issues; social, occupational and health care impact; barriers to recovery; and resources and strategies. Participants described a broad range of symptoms, most notably fatigue, cognitive difficulties, post-exertional crashes and psychological symptoms including depression and, in some cases, suicidal thoughts. These symptoms profoundly disrupted their social, working and family lives. In severe cases, independent living became impossible, with social isolation, severely reduced activity, and financial difficulties. Many described a long diagnostic journey in which symptoms were frequently dismissed as psychological and early advice to stay active that worsened their condition. The health care and social security systems were seen as ill-equipped to support people affected by Long Covid. With no effective causal therapies, treatment focused on symptom relief and participants tried many complementary and alternative treatments. Pacing was the only strategy widely used and perceived as effective in preventing crashes, alongside lifestyle adjustment, peer support, and maintaining hope. Conclusion These narrative accounts reveal the multidimensional burden of Long Covid, one that is exacerbated by how affected people are treated within the health and social systems. These findings underscore the need for empathic, knowledgeable care, validation of people’s experiences, and policy frameworks equipped to recognize and support people with Long Covid. Patient or Public Contribution This study is about the lived experiences of people affected by Long Covid. During the conceptualization phase, we consulted three people with lived experience of Long Covid to discuss the relevance of the research questions and study design. All participants received a newsletter with a plain language summary of interim findings. Following completion of this analysis, we conducted a focus group discussion with eight participants to validate our findings, identify gaps, and ensure that the findings accurately reflected their experiences. Feedback from this process informed the final manuscript.

papers.title: Hidden asymptomatic breakthrough infection in a proof-of-concept longitudinal study on SARS-CoV-2 vaccine recipients
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Individuals with asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection can unknowingly transmit the virus, yet identifying such subclinical infections in post-vaccinated populations remains challenging. Methods We conducted a longitudinal study of 129 infection-naïve vaccine recipients immunized with various combinations of SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) protein vaccine platforms. Sera were collected before the first dose ( v 1), at 2 weeks ( v 7) and 6 months ( v 8) after the third dose. Taiwan’s first major COVID-19 outbreak occurred between v 7 and v 8. We measured anti-nucleocapsid (anti-N) and anti-S IgG antibody titers by ELISA and assessed virus-neutralizing activity using live virus and pseudovirus assays. Results By developing an iterative serial screening method, we identified asymptomatic breakthrough (post-vaccination) infections among unconfirmed cases. Our v 7- v 8 paired cohort resolved into three distinct groups: confirmed cases (21%), asymptomatic breakthrough infections (17%), and uninfected subjects (62%). In normalized v 8 sera, confirmed cases exhibited an anti-S +++ (high) /anti-N +++ (high) phenotype, while uninfected subjects showed an anti-S + (low)/anti-N + (baseline) phenotype. Statistical analysis validated a distinct asymptomatic group characterized by an antibody profile anti-S ++ (intermediate) /anti-N + (baseline). Conclusions This approach may enable more accurate estimates of vaccine efficacy and infection prevalence. In a spike-vaccinated population, anti-N antibody is more a potential specific marker for COVID-19 symptomatic disease than an ideal marker for SARS-CoV-2 infection. To our knowledge, this is the first preliminary report of identification of asymptomatic breakthrough infection from a well-vaccinated population using self-matched longitudinal pairs of serum samples.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决在接种疫苗后人群中识别无症状 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的挑战,因为这些人可能在不知情的情况下传播病毒而不表现出症状。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 129 名未感染过 疫苗 的接受者进行了一项纵向研究,他们接受了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突 (S) 蛋白 疫苗 平台的各种组合的免疫。该研究的重点是追踪这些个体随时间的抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 在三个时间点收集血清:第一次给药前 (v1)、第三次给药后 2 周 (v7) 和 6 个月 (v8)。通过 ELISA 测量抗核衣壳(抗 N)和抗 S IgG 抗体滴度,并使用活病毒和假病毒测定评估病毒中和活​​性。统计分析验证了一个独特的无症状组,其特征是抗 S ++(中间)/抗 N +(基线)的抗体谱。
elements_zh.main_results: 通过开发迭代系列筛查方法,在未确诊病例中发现了无症状突破性感染。在标准化的 v8 血清中,确诊病例显示抗 S +++(高)/抗 N +++(高)表型,而未感染受试者则显示抗 S +(低)/抗 N +(基线)表型。队列研究 分为三个不同的组:确诊病例 (21%)、无症状突破性感染者 (17%) 和未感染者 (62%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究的方法通过使用自我匹配的纵向血清样本对来识别接种良好的人群中的无症状突破性感染,从而能够更准确地估计 疫苗 的疗效和感染情况。这是此类鉴定的第一份初步报告。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能会更准确地告知已接种疫苗的个体中 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的 监测 和 诊断,有助于更好地了解 疫苗 的有效性和无症状 传播 的动态。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于仅摘要分析,证据基于单个纵向 队列研究。由于摘要中缺乏详细的统计或临床验证,研究结果的可信度中等。
